name: Ancient Crunch

terms.couponNote: DELIBERATELY NULL, AND IT MUST STAY THAT WAY. The note carries 8% annual interest, which is easy to mistake for a preferred return. It is not: the interest does NOT pay in cash, it accrues and converts into additional equity at conversion. Typing it into the preferred-return column would invent eight years of cash that never arrives and would reclassify a venture position as an income sleeve, which changes the branch table used to price it. The interest is captured in the entry multiple instead.
terms.holdNote: Modelled at 3, which lands on 2029 — the middle of the memo's own 2028/2029/2030 exit grid. The founders target early 2028, having said 2027 will be the first clean full-year financial profile a buyer can underwrite; Spacestation call it 3-5 years. Management's own target is therefore the FASTEST of the three views and is not what is modelled.
terms.sponsorMoicNote: Taken from a specific cell of the memo's MOIC grid: a 2028 exit at $200M of revenue on a 3.5x EV/revenue multiple, which is 6.4x gross. That is the grid's most CONSERVATIVE revenue column paired with a multiple slightly below the ~3.8x average of the comparable exits Spacestation scraped. Two other anchors, for context: Braiden calls the bear corner of the grid — $200M at 2.5x, or 4.5x — the "absolute worst case", and separately guesses "5 to 10x" for his own money. The grid runs as high as 45.5x on a 2030 exit at $1B of revenue and 5.0x. 6.4x is used because this figure feeds the WINNER branch of the model, where the midpoint of an optimistic range would flatter the whole book.
terms.minimumNote: $5,000 minimum into the Spacestation SPV. Accredited investors only. GC allocation was $3,000,000 of a $10,000,000 round.
terms.feeNote: Spacestation SPV standard: 2% a year for 4 years, BILLED UPFRONT — so 8% comes off the top on day one — plus 20% carry. Fund investors get their own tier's discount. Note that the Spacestation FUND did not participate in the convertible note; that was SPV-only, so a fund holder has no exposure through that route.
terms.instrumentNote: $10,000,000 convertible promissory note: $100M pre-money valuation cap, 20% discount to the next priced round (investor takes whichever is better), 8% annual interest accruing to equity, 12-month maturity. A change of control while it is still DEBT pays the greater of 2x principal plus accrued interest or the as-converted value at the cap. That protection is temporary by design: once the note converts, the 2x and the 8% both stop and the holder is ordinary equity riding the upside. Closed 22 May 2026.
terms.entryMultipleNote: About 3.0x trailing 2025 revenue of $33M, or roughly 1.0x-1.25x against the $80M-$100M the company targets for 2026. Spacestation scraped ten comparable exits and found a median around 4x revenue, so the entry sits below where the category has historically cleared. Spacestation looked at this company in early 2023 and passed on valuation; they say this round is the first time the price worked.

pricedRound.note: The round the May 2026 convertible note was always a bridge to. $10M at a $245M PRE-money valuation, led by Bochy Ventures, roughly two months after the note closed — a 2.2x markup on paper in two months. Note holders are diluted about 10% and were offered pro rata. THOSE PRO RATA RIGHTS ARE A HANDSHAKE, NOT A CONTRACT: Spacestation tried to negotiate them and the company pushed back because it would complicate diligence with the lead. Seth Goldstein honoured it anyway and added up to $1M of allocation, open to holders taking more than their pro rata and to members who passed the first time. Because no contractual right exists, the pro rata figures were Spacestation's own estimates rather than a pro-forma cap table from the company's counsel. Anyone investing here is on the NEW terms at $245M, not the old $100M cap.

terms.whyTheNoteExisted: Ancient Crunch had a term sheet from a tier-1 consumer fund, signed March 2026 with a 90-day exclusivity that blocked every other conversation. At the one-yard line that investor said it wanted to see the manufacturing equipment running before funding — which was what the money was for. The convertible note was raised instead, quickly, to buy the equipment and to bring strategic consumer investors onto the cap table before a proper priced round. That is why the note's terms were, in Spacestation's own words, a “Black Friday” price rather than a market one.

uwScoreNote: 86 / 100, and it foots: 8.5 financial + 7.5 market + 8 product + 9 operations + 9 legal + 8 ESG + 9 team + 9 external validation + 9.5 exit + 8.5 deal structure. NOTE A CONFLICT: the 'last 8 deals' benchmark table in APEX_BRAIN records this deal at 88. The final scorecard sums to exactly 86, so 86 is carried here and the 88 is treated as a superseded earlier edition.
provisional: THERE ARE TWO ROUNDS IN THIS RECORD AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME INVESTMENT. (1) The CONVERTIBLE NOTE documented here, closed 22 May 2026 at a $100M pre-money cap. (2) A later PRICED round — $10M at a $245M PRE-money valuation led by Bochy Ventures, about two months after the note, a 2.2x markup on paper — with HANDSHAKE pro-rata offered to existing holders and no contractual right behind it. By then the company said it had reached profitability and taken Target national. The terms on this card are the NOTE's. If a position was taken in the priced round instead, the cap, the 20% discount, the 8% interest and the 2x change-of-control protection do NOT apply to it and the entry multiple is different. Check which one is held before relying on any figure here. Sourced from the pitch session, the underwrite Q&A, the deal snapshot, the final VC scorecard and the investor deck; no note document, subscription agreement or audited financial has been read. Completed 2026-09-28 with the 30 July priced-round session.
structure:
A house of brands making seed-oil-free salty snacks, fried in 100% grass-fed beef tallow with organic heritage grains. MASA is the tortilla chip and the flagship, Vandy the potato chip, and the popcorn brand launching in 2026 — called PERLA in the deal snapshot and on the pitch call, and GOLDEN AGE POPCORN in the investor deck's own TAM table and executive summary. The sources disagree; both names are carried so either resolves. Founded by Steven Rofrano (CEO, ex-Meta engineer, Yale) after frying the first batch in a turkey fryer in his parents' back garden, with Seth Goldstein (co-founder, President/CFO: Wharton, BCG, Bain Capital, Vector Capital, Summa Equity). Revenue ran $175K in 2022, $3M in 2023, $9M in 2024 and $33M in 2025, against an $80M-$100M target for 2026. The 2025 mix was roughly $23.2M DTC, $6.0M wholesale and $3.6M Amazon, so it is still a direct-to-consumer business that is only now becoming a retail one. DTC economics: $97 average order, 43% contribution margin, $115 blended CAC, and lifetime value of $265 at one year rising to $528 at three.

The central fact is MANUFACTURING. No contract manufacturer would fry in tallow — almost every chip line in the United States is kosher or vegan, and tallow is an animal fat that is solid at room temperature — so the company built its own, roughly $10M of capital for a line taking capacity from about 450,000 bags a month to around 3,000,000. COGS is expected to fall from about $3.50 a bag to under $1.00, with product margin approaching 90%. Management say the price could come down to roughly $4 on shelf and still leave a healthy business, while the product currently sells at $13 and leads its category, which is the clearest statement of brand power in the file.
keyRisks: THE MARGIN STORY IS A DTC MARGIN STORY. About 70% of 2025 revenue was direct-to-consumer, where you keep the whole margin. The growth case needs $200M-$450M of revenue and that can only come from retail, where the retailer takes a cut. Braiden says this plainly: the upside is not achievable as a DTC company, and whether the margin profile holds at national retail scale is the single unproven thing in the deal.

THE MANUFACTURING LINE HAD BEEN RUNNING FOR DAYS, NOT MONTHS, when this was underwritten. Corn was cooked for the first time the day before the pitch call. The entire COGS collapse from $3.50 to under $1.00 — which is most of why the entry price looks cheap — depends on that line ramping. It has not been seen at scale.

THERE IS NO MOAT IN THE ENGINEERING SENSE. No patents, no proprietary technology. Defensibility is brand, shelf placement, repeat purchase and a cost advantage from being first to build tallow capacity. Braiden names this as the central risk of the whole deal: whether someone can copy the product, brand it and get to shelf faster.

PREMIUM PRICING IS PROVEN IN THE NATURAL CHANNEL AND NOT IN MASS. Erewhon, Sprouts and Whole Foods are shoppers who will pay $13 for chips. Target has agreed to the same $12.99 and Walmart has not pushed on margin yet, but management concede Walmart will squeeze eventually. Club and mass are where the premium thesis is actually tested.

PRODUCT CONSISTENCY HAS BEEN A REAL PROBLEM, visible in online reviews, and it is the quietest risk in the file. It is attributed to hand-scale production and the new line is supposed to fix it. That is a reasonable expectation rather than a demonstrated outcome.

FOLLOW-ON DILUTION WAS FLAGGED AS POSSIBLE AND THEN HAPPENED, at about 10%. Management said on the pitch call that they did not anticipate raising again after this round. A priced round followed roughly two months later. The company's account is that this was always the plan and the note was bridge financing; either way, a note holder who does not take their pro rata is diluted.

QSBS IS NOT GUARANTEED. The investment begins as debt rather than stock, so the holding clock and the qualification tests depend on conversion and on the company staying compliant every year until exit. Eligibility at entry does not mean eligibility at exit.

DIET TRENDS MOVE. Tallow is having a moment and the company is deliberately not branded around it — the packaging says clean ingredients rather than beef fat, which makes a pivot easier. But the business is too young to have been observed through a shift in consumer sentiment.
THE $3B BEST CASE IS THE FOUNDER'S OWN NUMBER and he disclaims it in the same breath, saying the chance of hitting it is very low because founders are always excited. It is not a diligence figure.

THE PRO RATA IS A HANDSHAKE. Spacestation has no contractual pro-rata right in Ancient Crunch; the company pushed back and they accepted, on the strength of a relationship going back to when the founders were frying chips in a commercial kitchen. It was honoured this time and generously. It is not enforceable next time, and the later rounds are exactly where large growth investors ask for the whole allocation.
THE 2027 EBITDA FORECAST IS STATED TWO WAYS IN ONE CALL — $20M and $44M, minutes apart, unreconciled. On a business being valued off forward earnings that is a wide gap to leave open.
greenFlags: RETAIL VELOCITY, which is the strongest validation available in consumer packaged goods, and the company has it: 24.6 against a best-in-class benchmark of 14.8, at $13 a unit against a $5 benchmark. MASA is the number one selling tortilla chip at Sprouts, ahead of Siete, which exited to PepsiCo for $1.2B. At Erewhon it went from #18 to #1 in five months and is over half of all tortilla chip sales.
The company is in under 5% of US grocery shelf space, at roughly 2,000 doors against a 20,000 target, so the distribution story is early rather than mature.

RETAILERS WANT AN ALTERNATIVE TO FRITO-LAY, which holds 60-80% share depending on the chain and uses it to dictate terms. That is why Target, Walmart and Kroger are taking the meetings, and it is a structural tailwind rather than a sales achievement.

The deal structure is unusually investor-friendly: 8% accruing, a $100M cap, a 20% discount, and 2x principal plus interest ahead of common and preferred on a change of control while it is still debt.

A cap table and advisory bench that is hard to fault — Clayton Christopher, Brian Goldberg and Robbie Patterson of Asto Consumer Partners wrote the note with personal money after their firm judged the company too early for fund capital, which is a stronger signal than a fund cheque. Also Charles Coristine (CEO of LesserEvil, sold to Hershey for $750M), Michael Silverstein (BCG senior partner, author of Trading Up), Bill Weiland and Rodney McMullen, former CEO of Kroger.

A FOUNDER PAIR THAT COVERS BOTH HALVES OF THE PROBLEM: one obsessive about product, the other institutionally trained in finance and operations. The team's forecasting discipline is corroborated rather than asserted — Spacestation went back to the 2023 deck and found the revenue projections for 2026 were met and in places exceeded.

THE EXIT PATH IS THE BEST PART. There are essentially no independent, nationally distributed salty-snack brands, because they all get acquired: Siete $1.2B to PepsiCo, SkinnyPop $1.6B, LesserEvil $750M to Hershey, Simple Mills $795M to Flower Foods, Poppi $2.0B to PepsiCo, KIND $5.0B to Mars, Clif $2.9B to Mondelez. Bankers for two strategics have already made contact off the record.
source: Ancient Crunch pitch session and Spacestation underwrite Q&A (viewed 28 Sep 2026), the GC deal snapshot, the final VC scorecard (86/100), the Spring 2026 investor deck, and the 30 July 2026 pro-rata Q&A covering the later priced round. Figures are as presented in those materials. No note document, subscription agreement or audited financial has been read. The 30 July 2026 pro-rata session is now transcribed in full and folded in.

financials.ebitdaNote: Profitability was reached during 2026. EBITDA for 2026 is put at $5-6M, with most of the year unprofitable, which puts the $245M pre-money at roughly 30x current-year EBITDA — a revenue multiple is still the fairer lens this year. FOR 2027 THE SESSION GIVES TWO DIFFERENT NUMBERS IN THE SAME CALL: Jackson says $20M of EBITDA, and Sam says $44M a few minutes later. They are not reconciled and nobody on the call noticed. $20M is carried here because it is the lower, it is what the host stated directly in answer to the question, and it is the figure the valuation discussion was then built on. Treat $44M as unverified.
financials.capacityRoadmap: The $10M priced round funds capex to roughly $250M of revenue capacity. Another $10-15M after that would support around $750M, and Spacestation expect it to be self-funded from EBITDA rather than raised.

sections.title: Which round you hold — read this first
sections.body: There are TWO rounds in this record and they are not the same investment. The terms on this card are the MAY 2026 CONVERTIBLE NOTE's: a $100M pre-money cap, a 20% discount, 8% accruing interest and 2x your money ahead of everyone else if the company sells while the note is still debt. A PRICED ROUND followed about two months later at a $245M pre-money valuation led by Bochy Ventures, a 2.2x markup on paper, with roughly 10% dilution and pro rata offered on a handshake rather than a contract. If your position came from the priced round, none of the cap, the discount, the interest or the 2x protection applies to it and the entry multiple is different. Check which one you hold before relying on any figure here.
